paper.title: Metformin improves healthspan and lifespan in mice

organism.source_quote: Here we show that long-term treatment with metformin (0.1% w/w in diet) starting at middle age extends healthspan and lifespan in male mice, while a higher dose (1% w/w) was toxic.

strain.source_quote: We determined the long-term effects of two doses of metformin in male C57BL/6 mice.

sex.source_quote: Here we show that long-term treatment with metformin (0.1% w/w in diet) starting at middle age extends healthspan and lifespan in male mice, while a higher dose (1% w/w) was toxic.

sample_size.source_quote: n = 64 for metformin 0.1% group and n = 83 for their untreated counterparts

type.source_quote: Metformin is a drug commonly prescribed to treat patients with type 2 diabetes.

agent.source_quote: long-term treatment with metformin (0.1% w/w in diet) starting at middle age extends healthspan and lifespan in male mice

dose.source_quote: The first dose consisted of 0.1% metformin (w/w) supplemented in diet, which yielded a concentration of 0.45 ± 0.09 mM in serum

age_at_start.source_quote: The arrows at 54 weeks indicate the age at which metformin treatment was initiated.

mechanism.value: AMPK activation and increased antioxidant protection
mechanism.source_quote: At a molecular level, metformin increases AMP-activated protein kinase activity and increases antioxidant protection, resulting in reductions in both oxidative damage accumulation and chronic inflammation.

direction.source_quote: Diet supplementation with 0.1% metformin led to a 5.83% extension of mean lifespan (Fig. 1a)

mean_change_pct.source_quote: Diet supplementation with 0.1% metformin led to a 5.83% extension of mean lifespan (Fig. 1a)

p_value.source_quote: χ2 = 5.46 and p= 0.02 in Gehan-Breslow survival test

experiments.notes: Low-dose arm of a two-dose study; the high-dose (1% w/w) arm is recorded as a separate experiment with the opposite direction. A third longevity cohort in a different strain (B6C3F1 males, same 0.1% dose) gave a 4.15% mean extension that was not statistically significant (p = 0.064) and is not recorded as a separate experiment. Serum metformin 0.45 +/- 0.09 mM. Treatment lifelong from 54 weeks. Healthspan endpoints (rotarod, treadmill, open field, cataracts) also improved.

direction.source_quote: a higher concentration of the drug (1% w/w) was toxic and significantly shortened mean lifespan of C57BL/6 mice by 14.4% (Fig. 1b), likely due to renal failure

mean_change_pct.source_quote: a higher concentration of the drug (1% w/w) was toxic and significantly shortened mean lifespan of C57BL/6 mice by 14.4%

experiments.notes: High-dose arm: toxic, opposite direction to the 0.1% arm in the same paper. Authors attribute the shortened lifespan to renal failure; mechanism left null because this is a cause of toxicity, not a stated mechanism of action of the intervention on ageing. Serum metformin 5.03 +/- 0.87 mM, roughly ten-fold the low-dose exposure. Same start age (54 weeks) and strain as the low-dose arm.
